tools.name: audit_listing
tools.description: ASO audit of a live App Store or Google Play listing: each part (title, subtitle or short description, description, screenshots, ratings, localization) graded Working / Worth a look / Fix this with the reason, the listing's facts, and the biggest gaps. Rule-based, from the public listing.

tools.name: check_metadata
tools.description: Checks a draft title, App Store subtitle or Google Play short description, keyword field, description and promotional text against the store's rules: character limits, words repeated across fields, wasted keyword-field space, policy words. Use it on any listing copy you write or review. No store cal

tools.name: check_keyword_ranks
tools.description: Where an app ranks in the store's own search for up to 5 searches (top 50), with the apps on top. Without searches, checks the phrases its title and subtitle are written for.

tools.name: find_competitors
tools.description: The apps that rank above this one in the searches its listing is written for, with the searches each one tops.

tools.name: check_ai_visibility
tools.description: Asks ChatGPT (with web search) up to three generic questions a person would ask when looking for an app like this one, with the app's name left out (e.g. "What's the best app to learn a new language?"), and says whether it names the app, at what position, and which apps it recommends instead. Answer

tools.name: search_aso_guide
tools.description: Finds articles in the Appeak Pro ASO Guide for an App Store Optimization question (keywords, screenshots, ratings, localization, Google Play tags, AI discoverability...).

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "check_ai_visibility" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Asks ChatGPT (with web search) the question people ask when looking for an app like this one, e.g. "What's the best budget planner app?", and says whether it names the app, at what position, and which apps it recommends instead. One question on one assistant; answers are reused for a week." → after: "Asks ChatGPT (with web search) up to three generic questions a person would ask when looking for an app like this one, with the app's name left out (e.g. "What's the best app to learn a new language?"), and says whether it names the app, at what position, and which apps it recommends instead. Answer"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
